=== CONTRIBUTING.md (whole file) ===
Use Conventional Commit titles. Run `make check` before opening a PR.

=== $ git log --oneline -4 origin/main ===
3fa81c0 fix(deliver): send the signature header on redirects
c20de97 feat(endpoints): per-endpoint timeouts
91b6a4e chore: bump httpx
0be7731 docs: webhook signing

=== $ git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat ===
 courier/deliver.py    | 24 +++++++++++++++++++-----
 tests/test_deliver.py | 39 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 2 files changed, 58 insertions(+), 5 deletions(-)

=== $ git diff origin/main...HEAD -- courier/deliver.py ===
@@ -12,11 +12,28 @@
+MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3
+BACKOFF_BASE_S = 2
+
 def deliver(event, endpoint):
-    resp = post(endpoint.url, event.payload, timeout=endpoint.timeout)
-    return resp.status_code < 300
+    for attempt in range(MAX_ATTEMPTS):
+        resp = post(endpoint.url, event.payload, timeout=endpoint.timeout)
+        if resp.status_code < 300:
+            return True
+        if resp.status_code < 500:
+            return False          # a 4xx will not get better by retrying
+        time.sleep(BACKOFF_BASE_S ** attempt)
+    return False

=== what the chain ran earlier ===
$ make check
ruff: All checks passed!   mypy: Success   pytest: 52 passed in 2.9s

=== the commit message of the last commit ===
Retry 5xx deliveries up to 3 times (task 1); the dead-letter table is deferred, it needs a migration decision first

=== local review findings ===
[minor] courier/deliver.py:21 -- the final sleep after the last failed attempt is wasted (left open)

=== spec (.engineering/specs/wi_f60a27d3.md), what it says it will build ===
Why: support gets about 40 tickets a month from customers whose endpoint returned 503 during one of their deploys; the event is gone for good because `deliver()` tries once.
Approach: retry up to 5 times with exponential backoff, and write events that still fail to a new `dead_letters` table so support can replay them.
See also: spec id wi_f60a27d3.
expected_behavior: The description says what the diff does: 3 attempts (`MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3`), backoff base 2, no retry on a 4xx; it does not say 5 attempts
The description states under a scope-left-out heading or sentence that the `dead_letters` table was not built and why (it needs a migration decision), instead of presenting it as part of the change

The why is inlined (about 40 tickets a month from endpoints returning 503 during deploys) and the description does not rely on a link to or the id of the spec, and does not just restate the work item title
The description does not advocate for approval (no pitch that the change is safe, low-risk or ready to merge)
